title: [CLO Beginner's Tutorial] Materials_Lining and Edging
description: CLO Beginner's Guide, material-related series courses. chunks.content: ## Adding Sticky Layers to Collars and Collar Plates This section explains how to add and configure sticky layers on collars and collar plates in CLO, including selecting the correct sticky layer types and adjusting their physical properties. To add a sticky layer to the collar and collar plate: - Use the **Adjustment Plate Tool** to select both the collar and collar plate. - In the **Property Editor**, locate the sticky layer settings. - The plate will appear orange in the 2D or 3D window, indicating the sticky layer has been applied. - Under the **Physical Properties Preset** column, click the dropdown triangle to access six sticky layer types. - Select the appropriate sticky layer preset, for example, choose the "bottom collar" preset if working with a suit’s bottom collar. - Click **Details** under each preset to view or modify physical properties. Adding sticky layers here helps prevent seam line deformation, especially at the seam allowance. ## Extending and Customizing Sticky Layers on Seam Allowances This section covers extending sticky layers beyond pattern edges and setting their width and physical properties to prevent seam deformation. - Use the **Adjustment Plate Tool** and hold **Shift** to select multiple seam allowance lines. - In the **Property Editor**, select the sticky layer option and set the desired width. - If the sticky layer does not extend beyond the plate edge, use the extension controls: - Click the triangle on the left to extend the sticky layer. - Choose to extend it to the **opening** or the **end**; select **end** for full extension. - On the right triangle, select a physical properties preset for the sticky layer, similarly to the collar sticky layer. This process ensures the sticky layer covers the seam allowance fully, maintaining garment shape during simulation. ## Using the Sticky Layer Tool for Precise Placement and Editing This section details using the **Sticky Layer Tool** for adding, editing, and deleting sticky layers and managing their visibility in the 2D and 3D windows. - The **Sticky Layer Tool** is located above the sticker tool in the 2D toolbar. - Selecting this tool highlights existing sticky layers and their positions. - Click on any position to add a sticky layer, or quickly add multiple sticky layers by clicking multiple points. - To delete a sticky layer, select it using the tool and remove it. - Sticky layers can also be added partially within a closed inner shape of a pattern piece: - Switch to the **Adjustment Plate Tool**. - Click on the entire inner shape. - In the **Property Editor**, add a partial sticky layer. - To hide the orange sticky layer highlight in the 3D window, hover over the floating info display and close it. ## Adding Sticky Layers to Sleeves and Bottom Skirts This section explains two methods for adding sticky layers to sleeves and skirt bottoms, including using the sticky layer tool and sticky layer plates. - Select the **Sticky Layer Tool** in the 3D toolbar.

chunks.content: - Click on the entire inner shape. - In the **Property Editor**, add a partial sticky layer. - To hide the orange sticky layer highlight in the 3D window, hover over the floating info display and close it. ## Adding Sticky Layers to Sleeves and Bottom Skirts This section explains two methods for adding sticky layers to sleeves and skirt bottoms, including using the sticky layer tool and sticky layer plates. - Select the **Sticky Layer Tool** in the 3D toolbar. - Position the cursor over an empty edge line until a blue dot appears, indicating a valid sticky layer addition point. - Click to add a sticky layer at the desired point. - On the bottom line, use the middle mouse button to set the sticky layer direction. - Double-click to complete the sticky layer addition. - Sticky layers can be added and edited in both 2D and 3D windows by switching between the sticky layer and moving tools. ### Editing Sticky Layer Properties - In the **Property Editor**, set the sticky layer **Type** (inside, outside, or both sides). For example, set it to **inside**. - Adjust the **Width** and **Length** of the sticky layer, where length can be specified as a percentage of the original. - Modify particle diameter and conflict thickness values to fine-tune the sticky layer behavior. - Choose the sticky layer material from available materials in the **Object Window**. - Set the **Slash Line Direction** or input a specific slash line angle. ### Marking Sticky Layer Surfaces - Right-click on the side of the sticky layer to mark its surface. - You can initialize, counter-activate, freeze, or flip the surface as needed. ## Creating and Sewing Side Panels on Sleeves This section describes the creation of side panels on sleeves using the hook outline tool, and sewing them to ensure even seam lines. - Use the **Hook Outline Tool** and hold **Shift** to select a circular group of lines on the sleeve’s inner line (approximately 1 cm). - Right-click on the selection and choose **Hook as Panel**. - Move the side panel with the mouse and click the blank space to place it. - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to select the placed panel. - Press **Ctrl + D** to duplicate the side panel and place it on the opposite side. - Use the **Sewing Tool** to sew the side panels to the sleeve. ### Finalizing Side Seam - To ensure an even side seam, fold the seam line at the bottom. - Select the side panel in the 3D window. - Right-click and select **Add to Inside** to add the side panel inside the sleeve panel. - The side panel will align with the sewing line and fit the sleeve shape. ## Simulation and Completion After sewing and adjustments, run the simulation to check garment fit and seam integrity. Once stable, stop the simulation. The sleeve side panel and sticky layers are then finalized, completing the sleeve construction.
